title: Handball: coaching overview
d: Coaching Handball means teaching score more goals than the opponent within two 30-minute halves.
definition: Coaching Handball means teaching score more goals than the opponent within two 30-minute halves.
description: Coaching Handball is teaching people to achieve the objective — score more goals than the opponent — inside the constraints of two 30-minute halves and the laws of the game. The coach's job has four parts: design practices that build skill, manage people so they perform, make decisions under pressure, and develop athletes as people. This database covers all four, grounded in the real rules and demands of Handball: 7 per side.

facts.objective: score more goals than the opponent

title: Coaching philosophy
d: Great Handball coaches are teachers first: clear, demanding, and consistent.
definition: Great Handball coaches are teachers first: clear, demanding, and consistent.
description: A Handball coaching philosophy answers three questions: how we play, how we treat people, and what winning means here. Write it down in one page and live it — athletes detect hypocrisy instantly. The best philosophies are simple enough for a twelve-year-old to repeat and strong enough to guide a championship: effort, respect, and the courage to keep learning.

title: Teaching key rule 1
d: Teach Handball rule 1: Players may take 3 steps with the ball and hold it 3 seconds..
definition: Teach Handball rule 1: Players may take 3 steps with the ball and hold it 3 seconds..
description: Teaching Handball rule 1 — Players may take 3 steps with the ball and hold it 3 seconds. — works best in three steps: explain the reason (the unfair advantage it prevents), demonstrate it live, then drill it under pressure until compliance is automatic. Test understanding with scenarios, not quizzes: freeze a practice and ask what the call should be. Athletes who understand the why rarely need reminding of the what.

title: Designing sessions
d: A Handball session: warm-up, skill, tactical, conditioned game, cool-down.
definition: A Handball session: warm-up, skill, tactical, conditioned game, cool-down.
description: Design Handball sessions in five blocks: dynamic warm-up with the ball or implement, one skill focus, one tactical focus, a conditioned game that rewards the day's theme, and a cool-down with review. Plan 90 minutes and protect the plan — the loudest parent never outranks the session objective. Every drill answers: what will be better after this?

title: Giving feedback
d: Feedback in Handball: one thing, specific, immediate, then a retry.
definition: Feedback in Handball: one thing, specific, immediate, then a retry.
description: Feedback that changes Handball performance is specific, immediate, and limited to one thing: name what you saw, name the fix, and give a retry within seconds. Sandwich praise around corrections at a 3-to-1 ratio for young athletes; elite athletes can take it straight. Never coach the mistake you just praised away — pick your moment.

title: Motivating athletes
d: Motivate Handball players with autonomy, mastery, and belonging.
definition: Motivate Handball players with autonomy, mastery, and belonging.
description: Motivation in Handball lasts when it comes from inside: give athletes choices (autonomy), visible improvement (mastery), and a team worth belonging to. Carrots and sticks work for a week; purpose works for a career. Know what each athlete plays for — the answer differs, and coaching the individual beats coaching the roster.

title: Teaching tactics
d: Handball tactics: teach the shape walking before running.
definition: Handball tactics: teach the shape walking before running.
description: Handball tactics are taught walking, then jogging, then full speed, then live — skipping steps builds confusion that looks like disobedience. Use freeze-replay: stop the game at the decision moment and ask the player what they saw before telling them. Tactical understanding doubles when athletes scout opponents themselves.

title: Game management
d: Manage Handball games: know the score, the clock, and your bench.
definition: Manage Handball games: know the score, the clock, and your bench.
description: Game management in Handball is clock, score, and personnel: every decision weighs all three. Plan substitution windows and timeout triggers before the game, because pressure destroys improvisation. The best in-game coaches are boring — they execute the plan while opponents panic. Review every game against the plan within 24 hours.

title: Player development
d: Develop Handball athletes in stages: fundamentals, then position, then leadership.
definition: Develop Handball athletes in stages: fundamentals, then position, then leadership.
description: Long-term Handball development runs in stages: broad fundamentals first, positional craft second, leadership and game understanding third. Never sacrifice stage one for short-term wins — the twelve-year-old star built on tricks is the sixteen-year-old who quits. Track development in skills mastered, not trophies lifted.

title: Team culture
d: Culture beats strategy in Handball: set standards, enforce them equally.
definition: Culture beats strategy in Handball: set standards, enforce them equally.
description: Handball team culture is what players do when the coach is not watching. Set three to five non-negotiable standards — punctuality, effort, respect — and enforce them with stars and beginners identically. Culture is built in small moments: the senior who picks up cones, the apology after a bad foul. Protect it fiercely.

title: Season planning
d: Plan the Handball season: preseason, competition, and recovery blocks.
definition: Plan the Handball season: preseason, competition, and recovery blocks.
description: Season planning for Handball: preseason builds fitness and installs systems, the competition phase sharpens and maintains, and the off-season restores. Peak for the events that matter; treat the rest as rehearsal. Schedule lighter weeks before big competitions — tired teams make tired decisions.

title: Working with officials
d: Handball coaches manage officials with respect: ask, never argue.
definition: Handball coaches manage officials with respect: ask, never argue.
description: Officials in Handball respond to respect: captains ask questions, coaches never chase calls. Teach athletes that the call stands and the next play matters more. A coach who berates officials teaches athletes to blame — and loses the close calls that respect might have earned.

title: Safety and welfare
d: Handball safety: the coach is responsible for every athlete's welfare.
definition: Handball safety: the coach is responsible for every athlete's welfare.
description: Safety in Handball is the coach's first duty: safe venues and equipment, proper warm-ups, concussion protocols, and the courage to sit a star who is hurt. Welfare extends beyond the body — watch for burnout, anxiety, and the athlete who has gone quiet. No result justifies harming a young person.

title: Scouting opponents
d: Scout Handball opponents: tendencies, not just talent.
definition: Scout Handball opponents: tendencies, not just talent.
description: Scouting Handball opponents means finding tendencies: what they do under pressure, where their shape breaks, who takes the big moments. Give athletes two or three keys, not twenty — overloaded players play slow. Scout yourself too; your own tendencies are the opponent's scouting report.

title: Developing assistants
d: Great Handball head coaches build great assistants: delegate real responsibility.
definition: Great Handball head coaches build great assistants: delegate real responsibility.
description: Assistant coaches in Handball grow when given real ownership — a unit, a phase of practice, a scouting assignment — not just cones and water. Mentor deliberately: explain your decisions, invite challenge in private, and credit publicly. The program outlasts any one coach only if the next one is being built.

title: Coaching ethics
d: Handball ethics: the scoreboard never outranks the person.
definition: Handball ethics: the scoreboard never outranks the person.
description: Coaching ethics in Handball: never sacrifice an athlete's health, dignity, or future for a result. Play by the rules and the spirit of the rules; recruit honestly; cut players with compassion and clarity. The measure of a coach is not the trophy cabinet but the adults the athletes become.

title: Practice games
d: Conditioned Handball games teach faster than drills alone.
definition: Conditioned Handball games teach faster than drills alone.
description: Conditioned games in Handball — small-sided, with rules that reward the week's theme — transfer skills to matches better than isolated drills. Design the constraint so the desired behavior wins: want switching play? Award double for goals after a switch. Let them play; coach with questions at breaks, not commands during.

title: Working with parents
d: Youth Handball coaches: recruit the parents as allies, not adversaries.
definition: Youth Handball coaches: recruit the parents as allies, not adversaries.
description: Parents in youth Handball need a preseason meeting: your philosophy, playing-time policy, and the 24-hour rule for complaints. Most parent problems come from surprise — communicate early and often. Never discuss another child's playing time, and never let a parent coach from the sideline unchallenged.

title: Talent identification
d: Spot Handball talent: look for athleticism, attitude, and learning speed.
definition: Spot Handball talent: look for athleticism, attitude, and learning speed.
description: Talent identification in Handball weighs physical gifts, coachability, and love of the game over current skill — skills can be taught, attitude rarely changes. Watch how prospects handle failure and whether they improve between viewings. The best predictor of future performance is rate of learning, not present ability.

title: Mental training
d: Train the Handball mind: routines, self-talk, and pressure practice.
definition: Train the Handball mind: routines, self-talk, and pressure practice.
description: Mental training in Handball: teach a pre-performance routine, constructive self-talk, and visualization of successful execution. Simulate pressure in practice — consequences for misses, noise, scoreboard scenarios — so competition feels familiar. Confidence is built from preparation evidence, not pep talks.

title: Integrating fitness
d: Blend fitness into Handball skill work: fit players learn faster.
definition: Blend fitness into Handball skill work: fit players learn faster.
description: Fitness integration in Handball: embed conditioning inside skill drills rather than bolting on separate running — players stay engaged and learn tired, like matches demand. Keep pure fitness blocks short and purposeful. Monitor workload; the fittest team is the one that trains hardest without breaking.

title: Managing injuries
d: Injured Handball athletes need a plan, honesty, and patience.
definition: Injured Handball athletes need a plan, honesty, and patience.
description: Injury management in Handball: follow medical advice exactly, keep the athlete connected to the team, and set criteria-based return milestones — not dates. The re-injury risk peaks in the first month back; progress through controlled contact before full competition. Never let anyone — including the athlete — rush the process.

title: Video review
d: Handball video: short clips, one fix each, athletes involved.
definition: Handball video: short clips, one fix each, athletes involved.
description: Video review in Handball works in 15-minute blocks: three clips maximum, one fix per clip, and athletes analyzing before the coach speaks. Show good examples as often as errors — the brain copies what it sees celebrated. Team sessions build shared understanding; individual clips build personal accountability.

title: Pre-game preparation
d: Handball pre-game: same routine, clear roles, calm minds.
definition: Handball pre-game: same routine, clear roles, calm minds.
description: Pre-game preparation in Handball: a fixed timeline, a dynamic warm-up that ends at game intensity, equipment checks, and two or three tactical keys — no new information. The routine's job is to make the big game feel like every other game. Arrive early enough that nothing is rushed.

title: Post-game review
d: Review Handball games within 24 hours: facts first, feelings later.
definition: Review Handball games within 24 hours: facts first, feelings later.
description: Post-game review in Handball: wait for emotions to cool, then review against the game plan with video — what worked, what broke, one fix for training. Praise effort publicly, correct privately, and never humiliate. The review's product is next week's practice plan, not blame.
